title: Consistent perturbation expansions in screened interactions
authors: Abdallah Arthur El Sahili, Francesco Sottile, Lucia Reining
abstract: Many-body perturbation theory is a powerful framework to calculate spectroscopic quantities, as well as the total energy. However, the field suffers from the fact that different flavors of approximations lead to a wide range of results. We present several in principle exact expansions and discuss how to use them consistently. We concentrate on the first two orders in the respective screened Coulomb interaction. Of special interest is a consistent expansion around the Kohn-Sham system. We illustrate the performance of the various choices using the symmetric Hubbard dimer over a wide range of correlation strength. In particular, the expansion based on exact Kohn-Sham ingredients stands out as a promising route towards good energies and good spectra.
summary: This paper addresses the theoretical inconsistency plaguing many-body perturbation theory by developing systematic, order-by-order expansions for electronic structure calculations. By focusing on a consistent framework derived from screened interactions, the authors propose that using ingredients derived from the Kohn-Sham system offers a robust path toward accurate energy and spectral predictions.
main_problem: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) suffers from inconsistent results because different approximations lead to varying calculations for spectroscopic quantities and total energy.
main_result: The authors propose a consistent framework by deriving rigorous perturbation expansions, highlighting that the expansion based on exact Kohn-Sham ingredients is a promising route for accurate results.
method: The work involves deriving systematic, order-by-order expansions of the Dyson equation using screened Coulomb interactions ($W$) up to the second order.
model_or_system: The general many-body problem in condensed matter physics is studied, with the symmetric Hubbard dimer used as a specific model system for illustration.
key_observables: One-body Green's function ($G$), self-energy ($\Sigma$), total energy ($E_0$), and spectral functions ($A(\omega)$).
important_parameters: Correlation strength, the screened interaction $W$, and the order of the perturbation expansion (up to second order).
main_assumptions: The authors focus on defining consistency by using a self-contained diagrammatic series, explicitly avoiding complex issues like self-consistency loops or Bethe-Salpeter equation approximations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the Dyson equation, introduces screening via $W$, develops the perturbation theory for the self-energy ($\Sigma^{(1)}, \Sigma^{(2)}$), and discusses methods for calculating $G$ from $\Sigma$ to ensure theoretical consistency.
why_interesting: The focus on systematic, rigorous diagrammatic expansions and the need for consistent approximations in correlated electron systems directly relates to advanced many-body physics techniques used in AMO and quantum optics.
